Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 12, verse 19:

﴿And there came a caravan﴾. They were a company of travelers. They were called sayyarah (caravan) because they travel (yasir) in the land. They were a company (rufqah) from Madyan heading to Egypt, but they lost their way and camped near the well. The well was in a remote desert (qafr ba'id), far from habitation, for shepherds and passers-by. Its water was brackish (malihan), but it became sweet when Yusuf, peace be upon him, was thrown into it. When they stopped, they sent a man from the people of Madyan called Malik ibn Du'r (Du'r, with the letter dal unpointed) to seek water. This is the meaning of His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So they sent their water-drawer﴾. The warid (water-drawer) is the one who goes ahead of the company to the water and prepares the ropes and buckets.

﴿So he let down his bucket﴾, that is, he sent it into the well. It is said: adlaytu al-dalw means I lowered the bucket into the well, and dalawtuha means I drew it up. Yusuf caught hold of the rope, and when he came out, behold, he was a boy of the utmost beauty.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yusuf was given half of beauty" (ﷺ).[[A part of the hadith of the Night Journey (al-Isra'), narrated by Muslim in al-Iman, chapter on the Night Journey of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, no. (162): 1/145-147, and in it: "... and behold, Yusuf ﷺ, to whom had been given half of beauty." The hadith is also narrated with the author's wording by Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Hakim, and al-Wahidi in his Tafsir. See Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah: 3/470; Kashf al-Khafa wa Muzil al-Ilbas: 1/160-161; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/203; al-Matalib al-'Aliyah: 3/273; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/531.]]

It is said that he inherited that beauty from his grandmother Sarah, who had been given a sixth of beauty.

Ibn Ishaq said: Yusuf and his mother took two-thirds of beauty.[[Al-Albani said: this is munkar and baseless with this wording, as it contradicts the sound hadith, and its chain is extremely weak. See the previous references.]]

When Malik ibn Du'r saw him, ﴿he exclaimed, "Good news!"﴾. Most readers recited it thus, with an alif and a fatha on the ya', meaning the water-drawer gave good news to his companions, saying: "Rejoice!" The people of Kufa recited "Ya bushra" without an idafah, meaning the water-drawer called out to a man among his companions named Bushra.

﴿This is a boy﴾. Ibn Mujahid narrated from his father that the walls of the well wept for Yusuf when he was brought out of it.

﴿And they concealed him﴾, that is, they hid him, ﴿as merchandise﴾. Mujahid said: Malik ibn Du'r and his companions among the merchants who were with them concealed him, and they said: "He is merchandise which some people of the water entrusted to us to bring to Egypt, lest they be asked to share in him."

It is also said: he meant that Yusuf's brothers concealed the matter of Yusuf and said: "This is a slave of ours who ran away."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah knows what they do﴾. Then Yahudha came to Yusuf with food but did not find him in the well, so he informed his brothers. They searched for him, and behold, they found Malik and his companions had stopped, so they came to them and found Yusuf. They said, "This is a runaway slave of ours." It is said that they threatened Yusuf until he did not know his state, and he said the same as they said. Then they sold him. This is the meaning of His words, Mighty and Majestic:

﴿They sold him﴾ i.e., they sold him, ﴿for a paltry price﴾. Al-Dahhak, Muqatil and al-Suddi said: "It was unlawful, because the price of a free man is unlawful, and the unlawful is called paltry (bakhs) because it is stripped of blessing."

From Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud: "Bakhs means debased (zuyuf), i.e., counterfeit coins."

Ikrimah and al-Sha'bi said: "For a small price."

﴿Dirhams﴾ is a substitute for "price". ﴿Counted﴾: the use of the number is an expression of their small quantity.

It was also said: "He said 'counted' because in that era they did not weigh anything less than forty dirhams. They would count them by number, and when they reached an ounce (uqiyyah), they would weigh them."

They differed over the number of those dirhams. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and Qatadah said: "Twenty dirhams, which they divided between themselves, two dirhams each."

Mujahid said: "Twenty-two dirhams."

Ikrimah said: "Forty dirhams."[[Imam Abu Ja'far al-Tabari said in his Tafsir (exegesis), (16/15-16): "The correct position on this is to say: God, exalted is He, informed that they sold him for counted dirhams, not weighed, and the amount was not specified by weight or number, nor is there any evidence in a book or in a report from the Messenger (ﷺ) establishing it. It is possible that it was twenty, and it is possible that it was twenty-two, and that it was forty, or less or more than that. Whichever it was, they were counted and not weighed, and knowing the exact weight of it yields no benefit that bears on religion, nor does ignorance of it bring any harm. Belief in the apparent meaning of the revelation is obligatory, and whatever lies beyond that is set aside from us as a burden of knowledge."]]

﴿And they were﴾, i.e., the brothers of Joseph, ﴿regarding him﴾, i.e., regarding Joseph, ﴿among those who were indifferent﴾, because they did not know his station with God.

It was also said: "They were indifferent regarding the price, because their aim was not to obtain the price; their aim was only to keep Joseph far from his father."

Then Malik ibn Dhu'r and his companions set off with Joseph, and his brothers followed them, saying: "Secure him, so that he does not run away." He said: "So they took him away until they arrived in Egypt, and Malik offered him for sale, and Qitfir bought him," so said Ibn Abbas.

It was also said: "Ithfir, the official in charge of the king's affairs, who was over the treasuries of Egypt, was called al-Aziz. The king in Egypt and its surroundings at that time was al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid ibn Shirwan, of the Amalekites."

It was also said: "This king did not die until he believed and followed Joseph in his religion; then he died while Joseph was still alive."

Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: "When they entered Egypt, Qitfir met Malik ibn Dhu'r and bought Joseph from him for twenty dinars, a pair of sandals, and two white garments."

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "The caravan came to Egypt with Joseph. They took him into the market to offer him for sale, and people bid against one another over his price, until his price reached his weight in gold, his weight in silver, his weight in musk and silk. His weight was four hundred ratl, and he was thirteen years old. Qitfir bought him from Malik ibn Dhu'r for this price." That is the meaning of His, exalted is He, saying:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 12, verse 21:

﴿The one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife: "Make his residence comfortable."﴾ Her name was Ra'il, and it is said: Zulaykha. ﴿Make his residence comfortable﴾ means his dwelling and his stay, and al-mathwa is the place of residence.

It is also said: honour him in his food, his clothing and his lodging.

Qatada and Ibn Jurayj said: his station (manzilatahu).

﴿It may be that he will benefit us﴾ means: we will sell him at a profit if we want to sell him, or he will suffice us when he reaches some of our affairs.

﴿Or we may take him as a son﴾ means: we will adopt him.

Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The most perceptive of people are three: the al-Aziz regarding Yusuf, when he said to his wife, "Make his residence comfortable, it may be that he will benefit us"; the daughter of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) when she said to her father about Musa (peace be upon him), "O father, hire him"; and Abu Bakr regarding Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) when he appointed him as successor [[Authenticated by al-Hakim according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed, al-Mustadrak: 2/346. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/268): "Al-Tabarani narrated it with two chains, and the narrators of one of them are the narrators of the authentic collections if Muhammad ibn Kathir is al-Abdi; and if he is al-Thaqafi, then he was deemed trustworthy despite considerable weakness in him."]].

﴿And thus We established Yusuf in the land﴾ [i.e., in the land of Egypt] [[Omitted from "B".]] means: just as We rescued Yusuf from being killed and brought him out of the well, so too We established him in the land, and made him over its treasuries.

﴿And that We may teach him the interpretation of events﴾ means: We established him in the land so that We may teach him the interpretation of events, and this is an expression for dreams.

﴿And Allah is dominant over His affair﴾ It is said: the pronoun in amrihi (His affair) refers to Allah the Exalted, meaning: Allah is dominant over His affair, He does what He wills; nothing overcomes Him, and no one can reverse His judgment.

It is also said: it refers back to Yusuf (peace be upon him), meaning: Allah has authority over Yusuf's affair through management and encompassing care [in "B": "and comprehensive care"], not leaving him to anyone until he reaches the limit of His knowledge concerning him.

﴿But most of the people do not know﴾ what Allah is doing with him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 12, verse 22:

﴿When he reached his full strength﴾ — that is, the limit of his youth, vigour and power. Mujahid said: thirty-three years.

al-Suddi said: thirty years.

al-Dahhak said: twenty years.

al-Kalbi said: al-ashudd (full strength) is the span from eighteen years of age to thirty years.

Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about al-ashudd, and he said: it is the age of maturity (al-hulm).[[Al-Imam al-Tabari said (16/23): "The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: Allah informed that He gave Yusuf, when he reached his full strength, judgement and knowledge. Al-ashudd is the attainment of his strength and youth. It is permissible that He gave him that when he was eighteen years old, and it is permissible that He gave it to him when he was twenty years old, and it is permissible that He gave it to him when he was thirty-three years old. There is no indication of it in the Book of Allah, nor a report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor in the consensus of the Community, as to which of these it was. Since that is not established from the aspect I have mentioned, the correct position is to say about it what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said, until a proof is established by the soundness of what has been said on this matter from a channel that must be accepted, and then it is accepted."]]

﴿We gave him judgement and knowledge﴾ — as for judgement (hukm), it is prophethood; and knowledge ('ilm) is understanding (fiqh) in the religion.

It was also said: "judgement" means correctness in speech; and "knowledge" means the interpretation of dreams.

It was also said: the difference between the hakim (wise person) and the 'alim (knowing person) is that the 'alim is one who knows things, while the hakim is one who acts in accordance with what knowledge requires.

﴿Thus do We reward the doers of good﴾ — Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: the believers. And from him also: the guided ones. al-Dahhak said: those who are patient in calamities, just as Yusuf, peace be upon him, was patient.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 12, verse 23:

﴿And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him from himself﴾, meaning: the wife of al-'Aziz. Al-murawadah (seeking to seduce, lit. seeking the act): seeking the deed. What is meant here is that she invited him to herself so that he would lie with her. ﴿And she closed the doors﴾, meaning: she locked them tight, and there were seven of them. ﴿And she said: Hayt laka﴾, meaning: come on and approach.

The people of Kufa and Basra recited ﴿Hayta laka﴾ with a fatha on the ha and the ta.

The people of Madina and Syria recited ﴿Hiyta﴾ with a kasra on the ha and a fatha on the ta.

Ibn Kathir recited ﴿Hayta﴾ with a fatha on the ha and a damma on the ta.

Al-Sulami and Qatadah recited ﴿Hi'tu laka﴾ with a kasra on the ha and a damma on the ta, with hamza, meaning: I have prepared myself for you. Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i denied this reading and said: this has not been related from the Arabs.

The first (reading) is the one well known among the Arabs.

Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) recited to me ﴿Hayta laka﴾ [[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/346, and he declared it sound according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim. See also: Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/30-31 with the note of Shaykh Mahmud Shakir.]].

Abu 'Ubaydah [[In "B": Abu 'Ubayd. See also: Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah 1/305.]] said: al-Kisa'i used to say: it is a dialect of the people of Hawran, transferred to the Hijaz, its meaning being [to me] [[Addition from "B".]] "come here."

'Ikrimah said: it is also in the Hawrani dialect, meaning "come."

Mujahid and others said: it is an Arabic dialect and it is a word of urging and of turning towards something.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: the Arabs do not form a dual, plural or feminine of ﴿Hayta﴾; it takes one form in every case.

﴿He said﴾ to her at that point: ﴿Allah forbid!﴾, meaning: I seek refuge in Allah and I hold fast to Allah from what you call me to. ﴿Indeed, He is my Lord﴾, meaning that your husband Qitfir [[In Tafsir al-Tabari: (Itfir).]], my master, ﴿has made my stay good﴾, meaning: has made my dwelling honourable. This is the saying of most of the exegetes.

It has also been said: the pronoun refers to Allah, the Exalted, meaning: Allah, the Exalted, is my Lord, He has made my stay good, i.e., He sheltered me, and He saved me from the trial of the well.

﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers do not prosper﴾, meaning: if I did this and betrayed him regarding his family after he had honoured my stay, then I would be a wrongdoer, and the wrongdoers do not prosper.

It has also been said: ﴿the wrongdoers do not prosper﴾, i.e., adulterers do not attain happiness.

﴿Wa-laqad hammat bihi wa-hamma biha﴾ [And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her]. Al-hamm (intention, inclination) is approaching an action without actually entering into it. So her hamm was her resolve upon disobedience and fornication.

As for his hamm, it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "He untied the hamyan (money belt) and sat with her in the position of one who betrays." [[Narrated by Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya from Ibn 'Abbas as a mawquf (companion's statement). See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/521. The commentary on these narrations will come shortly.]]

And from Mujahid, who said: "He untied his sarawil (trousers) and began to work at his garments." This is the view of most of the earlier scholars, such as Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan. [[As-Suyuti cited these narrations from them in al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/521-522.]]

Al-Dahhak said: "Shaytan moved between them, striking one of his hands against the neck of Yusuf and the other against the neck of the woman, until he brought them together."

Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam said: "Some people have denied this view, but the correct view is what the earlier scholars of this community said, for they were too knowledgeable about Allah to say such things about the prophets, peace be upon them, without knowledge."

As-Suddi and Ibn Ishaq said: "When the wife of the ruler desired to seduce Yusuf, peace be upon him, into herself, she began to mention to him the excellent qualities of his person and to arouse his desire for herself. She said: 'O Yusuf, how beautiful is your hair!'

He said: 'It is the first thing that will fall out of my body.'

She said: 'How beautiful are your eyes!' He said: 'They are the first thing that will flow down over my face in my grave.'

She said: 'How beautiful is your face!'

He said: 'It is for the dust to devour.' [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/34.]]

It is also said that she said: 'Indeed, a silken bed is spread out. Rise and fulfil my need.'

He said: 'Then my share of Paradise would be lost.'

She continued to tempt him and to invite him to pleasure, while he was a young man who felt the ardour of youth that a man feels, and she was a beautiful, attractive woman. Until he inclined toward her because of what he saw of her eagerness, and he had the hamm (intention) toward her. Then Allah, the Exalted, rescued His servant and prophet by the proof that He mentioned. [[Narrated by al-Tabari in the same place.]]

Some later scholars claimed that this does not befit the condition of the prophets, peace be upon them. [[Ibn 'Atiyya suggested a view that this did not occur in the state of prophethood. He said in al-Muharrar al-Wajiz (7/477-478): "What I say about this verse is: that Yusuf being a prophet at the time of this incident is not established, and no narration supports it. If that is so, then he was a believer who had been given judgment and knowledge, and it is permissible for him to have the hamm which is the desire for a thing without committing it, and to entertain a bad thought, with the sin that this involves. And if we suppose him to be a prophet at that time, then in my view only the hamm that is a passing thought is permissible for him, and nothing of what has been mentioned of untying a girdle or the like is correct for him, because prophethood entails infallibility. As for what has been related, that it was said to him: 'You will be recorded among the prophets and yet you act like the foolish,' its meaning is only the promise of prophethood later on. Hamm toward a thing has two levels: the first may occur for a prophet, while the second and greater level occurs only with a non-prophet, because continuing with a thought of disobedience and enjoying it is itself a disobedience that is recorded..." Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya said in Daqa'iq al-Tafsir (3/272-273): "Hamm is a generic term that includes two types, as Imam Ahmad said: 'Hamm is of two kinds: the hamm of passing thoughts and the hamm of persistence.' It is established in the Sahih from the Prophet ﷺ that when a servant intends an evil deed it is not recorded against him, and if he leaves it for Allah's sake, a good deed is recorded for him... Yusuf had a hamm, and he left it for Allah's sake, which is why Allah turned away from him evil and indecency because of his sincerity... As for what is transmitted, that he untied his trousers and sat in the position of a man with a woman, and that he saw the image of Ya'qub biting his hand, and similar things, all of it is what Allah and His Messenger did not report. Whatever is not so is taken from the Jews, who are among the greatest of people in lying about the prophets and slandering them, and every Muslim who transmitted it transmitted it from them. Not a single word of this was transmitted from our Prophet ﷺ."]] He said: The speech is complete at His saying: ﴿Wa-laqad hammat bihi﴾ [And she certainly desired him]. Then he began the report about Yusuf, peace be upon him, saying: ﴿Wa-hamma biha law la an ra'a burhana rabbihi﴾ [and he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord], with inversion, meaning: had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have desired her. But he saw the proof, so he did not desire her.

The grammarians rejected this and said: The Arabs do not place law la (had it not been for) after the verb. So one does not say: "Qumtu law la Zayd" [I would have stood up had it not been for Zayd], meaning "Law la Zayd laqumtu" [Had it not been for Zayd, I would have stood up]. [[In "B": hammat. The following bracketed words are omitted from "B".]]

It is also said: She desired to take him to bed, and he desired her, meaning he wished that she would be his wife.

This interpretation and similar ones are not acceptable, because they contradict the sayings of the earlier scholars from whom religion and knowledge are taken. [[The scholar al-Shinqiti said in his tafsir Adwa' al-Bayan: Tafsir al-Qur'an bi-l-Qur'an (3/60-62): "The second answer, which is the choice of Abu Hayyan, is that Yusuf never had any hamm at all, but it is negated because the proof was present. This view chosen by Abu Hayyan and others is the most consistent with the rules of the Arabic language, because it is common in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech for the omitted response to be preceded by something that indicates it, as in His saying: 'Upon Him rely, if you are Muslims' [5:23], meaning: if you are Muslims, then rely upon Him. The first clause is the indicator of the omitted response, not the response itself, because the responses of conditionals and of law la cannot precede them, but what is mentioned before them serves as an indicator, like the verse cited. And like His saying: 'Say: Bring your proof, if you are truthful' [2:111], meaning: if you are truthful, then bring your proof. According to this view, the meaning of the verse is: 'And he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord,' that is, had he not seen it, he would have desired her. So what precedes law la is the indicator of the omitted response, as is common in the Qur'an and the language. A parallel is His saying: 'It had almost disclosed it, had We not fortified her heart' [28:10]: what precedes law la is the indicator of the response, meaning: had We not fortified her heart, she would have disclosed it. Know that a group of Arabic scholars permitted placing the response of law la before it, and placing the response before the conditional in all conditionals. According to this view, the response of law la in His saying 'had he not seen the proof of his Lord' is what precedes it, namely 'and he desired her.' This permission of prior placement was held by the Kufans and by prominent Basrans such as Abu al-'Abbas al-Mubarrad and Abu Zayd al-Ansari." Shaykh Abu Hayyan al-Andalusi said in al-Bahr al-Muhit (5/294-295) the following: "The commentators have gone at length in explaining these two hammat, and some of them attributed to Yusuf what may not be attributed even to ordinary sinners. What I choose is that Yusuf, peace be upon him, never had the hamm for her at all, but it is negated because the seeing of the proof existed, just as you say: 'You would have departed, had Allah not protected you,' and you do not say that the response of law la precedes it, although no evidence prevents that. Rather, the explicit operative conditional particles differ regarding whether their responses may precede them, and the Kufans held that, as did prominent Basrans Abu Zayd al-Ansari and Abu al-'Abbas al-Mubarrad. Indeed we say that the response of law la is omitted because what precedes it indicates it, as the majority of the Basrans say regarding the Arabs' saying: 'You are a wrongdoer if you do it,' so they estimate it as: 'If you do it, then you are a wrongdoer,' and his saying 'You are a wrongdoer' does not establish wrongdoing, but it is affirmed upon the supposition of the act's occurrence. Likewise here the estimate is: 'Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have desired her,' so the existence of the desire depended on the supposition that the seeing of the proof was absent, but he did see the proof, so the desire was negated." After refuting al-Zajjaj with a linguistic objection, he said: "As for the statements of the early scholars, some of which al-Imam al-Baghawi cited here, we believe that nothing of that is authentically reported from any of them, because they are mutually contradictory statements, some of which refute others, and they are damaging even to ordinary sinful Muslims, let alone those who are definitively attested to be protected from sin. What is reported from the early scholars is not supported by the speech of the Arabs, because they estimated the response of law la as omitted with no evidence indicating it, since they did not estimate 'and he desired her,' and the speech of the Arabs does not indicate that the omitted element is of the meaning of what precedes the conditional, because what precedes the conditional is the indicator of it, and nothing is omitted without an indicator." Then Abu Hayyan says: "We have purified this book of ours, that is his tafsir al-Bahr al-Muhit, from transmitting what is found in the books of tafsir that is not fitting to mention, and have limited ourselves to what the language of the Arabs indicates and the context of the verses in this surah which show infallibility and the innocence of Yusuf, peace be upon him, from everything that disgraces." See also: al-Isra'iliyyat wa-l-Mawdu'at by Muhammad Muhammad Abu Shahba, pp. 307-319; Tafsir al-Manar by Muhammad Rashid Rida: 12/280-286.]]

Some have said: The degree that Yusuf, peace be upon him, committed was among the minor sins, and minor sins may occur for prophets, peace be upon them. [[See above, p. 218, footnote (5).]]

It is narrated that when Yusuf, peace be upon him, entered before the king when he came out of prison, and the woman had confessed, Yusuf said: ﴿That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret﴾ [12:52]. Jibril said to him: "Nor when you had the hamm for her, O Yusuf?" Thereupon Yusuf said: ﴿And I do not declare my soul innocent﴾ [12:53], and the rest of the verse. [[This is not the speech of Yusuf, peace be upon him, but rather the speech of the wife of the ruler, as the Qur'an clearly indicates, which no one who reflects upon the Qur'an can doubt. Allah, the Exalted, said: "And the king said: 'Bring him to me.' But when the messenger came to him, he said: 'Return to your lord and ask him about the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot.' [The king] said: 'What was your situation when you sought to seduce Yusuf?' They said: 'Allah forbid! We know of no evil from him.' The wife of the ruler said: 'Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed he is of the truthful.' [Yusuf said:] 'That is so he may know that I did not betray him in secret, and that Allah does not guide the plot of the betrayers. And I do not declare my soul innocent; indeed, the soul is incessantly commanding to evil, except those upon whom my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.'" [12:50-53] This is the speech of the wife of the ruler. Yusuf at that time was in prison and had not yet come before the king, nor had he heard his words or seen him. But when his innocence became manifest in his absence, as the wife of the ruler said: "That is so he may know that I did not betray him in secret," meaning: I did not betray him during his absence, although I had sought to seduce him in his presence. Then "the king said: 'Bring him to me, that I may take him for myself.' And when he spoke with him, he said: 'Indeed, today you are with us established and trusted.'" [12:54]. Many commentators have said that this is the speech of Yusuf. Some mentioned only this view, and it is a view of utmost corruption, with no evidence for it; rather the evidence indicates the opposite. See: Daqa'iq al-Tafsir by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya: (3/273).]]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Allah, the Exalted, did not mention the sins of the prophets, peace be upon them, in the Qur'an in order to reproach them, but mentioned them to show the place of blessing upon them, and so that no one would despair of His mercy." [[Yusuf, peace be upon him, is not described by Allah, the Exalted, as having committed a sin, and He, glorified is He, never mentions a sin of any prophet without mentioning his seeking forgiveness for it. He did not mention that Yusuf sought forgiveness for that word, just as He did not mention that he sought forgiveness for the preliminaries of indecency. So it is known that he did not commit a sin in this or that; rather, what he did was among the accepted good deeds and the thanked endeavours. See: Daqa'iq al-Tafsir: (3/262, 280).]]

It is also said: "He tested them with sins so that He might single out for purity and honour the one who meets all creation on the Day of Resurrection in a state of being humbled by disobedience."

It is also said: "So that He might make them leaders for the people of sin, in hope of mercy, and so that they would not despair of forgiveness and pardon."

Some of the people of spiritual realities said: "Hamm is of two kinds: a firm hamm, which is when it is accompanied by resolve, binding intent, and consent, like the hamm of the wife of the ruler, and the servant is held accountable for it; and a passing hamm, which is a fleeting thought and self-talk without choice or resolve, like the hamm of Yusuf, peace be upon him. So the servant is not held accountable for it as long as he does not speak or act upon it."

Abu 'Ali Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad Mahmish al-Ziyadi told us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan told us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami told us: 'Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ma'mar told us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, told us, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: When My servant speaks of doing a good deed, I write it for him as a good deed so long as he has not done it; when he does it, I write it for him as ten times its like. And when he speaks of doing an evil deed, I forgive it for him so long as he has not done it; when he does it, I write it for him as its like." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tawhid, chapter "(They wish to change the words of Allah)": 8/198; and in al-Riqaq, chapter "Whoever has the hamm of a good deed," from Ibn 'Abbas: 7/178; and Muslim in al-Iman, chapter "When the servant has the hamm of a good deed, it is recorded; and when he has the hamm of an evil deed, it is not recorded," no. (205): 1/117, through the chain of 'Abd al-Razzaq of the Sahifa of Hammam ibn Munabbih. See: al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq, Kitab al-Jami': 11/287, and through him al-Baghawi narrated it in Sharh al-Sunna: 14/337-338. See also: Sahifat Hammam ibn Munabbih, edited by Dr. Rif'at Fawzi, pp. 188-189.]]

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Law la an ra'a burhana rabbihi﴾ [had he not seen the proof of his Lord]. They differed about that proof. Qatada and most commentators said: He saw the image of Ya'qub, who was saying to him: "O Yusuf, will you do the deed of the foolish while you are recorded among the prophets?"

Al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, 'Ikrima, and al-Dahhak said: The ceiling of the house opened for him, and he saw Ya'qub, peace be upon him, biting on his finger. [[See the narrations from them in: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/521-523.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): Ya'qub (peace be upon him) was shown to him, and he struck his hand against his chest, and his desire came out through his fingertips [[If the desire came out of him, then there is no merit in his refraining from intending it, had it occurred from him.]].

As-Suddi said: It was called out, "O Yusuf, do it! Your likeness, so long as you do not do it, is that of a bird in the midst of the sky, which cannot be reached. But your likeness, if you do it, is his likeness when he dies and falls to the ground, unable to ward off [anything] from himself. And your likeness, so long as you do not do it, is that of a stubborn bull which cannot be approached; but your likeness, if you do it, is the likeness of a bull that dies, so that ants enter at the base of its horns, unable to repel them from itself."

And from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), concerning His words ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her﴾: he untied his trousers and sat down between her legs as a man sits with his wife. Then suddenly a palm appeared between them, without wrist or upper arm, with writing upon it: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know whatever you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10–11]. So he got up and fled, and she got up too. When the terror had left them, she returned and he returned, and that palm appeared again with writing upon it: ﴿And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse; indeed, it is ever an immorality and an evil way﴾ [al-Isra': 32]. So he got up and fled, and she got up too. When the terror had left them, she returned and he returned, and it appeared, and he saw that palm with writing upon it: ﴿And fear a Day on which you will be returned to Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 281]. So he got up and fled, and she got up too. When the terror had left them, she returned and he returned. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said to Jibril (peace be upon him): "Overtake My servant before he commits the sin." So Jibril (peace be upon him) descended, biting on his finger, saying: "O Yusuf, will you act like the foolish, while you are recorded with Allah among the prophets?" [[And were these noble verses revealed to anyone before our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)?]].

It is also narrated that he (Jibril) wiped him with his wing, and his desire came out through his fingertips.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Yusuf raised his head toward the ceiling of the house when he intended her, and he saw a writing on the wall of the house: "Do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse; indeed, it is ever an immorality and an evil way."

'Atiyyah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "In the proof" means that he saw the image of the king [[For the takhrij of these narrations, see: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/521–524.]].

Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "The proof" is the prophethood which Allah placed in his breast, which came between him and what displeases Allah, mighty and majestic [[Close to this view is the statement of those who said: the proof was that he knew what Allah had made lawful and what He had made unlawful, so he saw the prohibition of fornication; this is related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi. Ibn Qutaybah said: he saw the proof of Allah against him, which is the "burhan." Ibn al-Jawzi said in Zad al-Masir (4/209): "This is the correct view, and what preceded it is nothing; these are only narrations of the storytellers, and I have pointed out their corruption in my book al-Mughni fi al-Tafsir. How can one suppose of a noble prophet of Allah that he would be frightened, terrified, and compelled to abandon this disobedience while he was persisting in it? This is the utmost ugliness!"]].

It is related from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: There was an idol in the house, so the woman got up and covered it with a cloth. Yusuf said to her: "Why did you do this?"

She said: "I felt shy before it, that it would see me in disobedience."

Yusuf said: "Are you ashamed before what does not hear, does not see, and does not understand? I have more right to be ashamed before my Lord." And he fled [[Imam Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said in his tafsir (16/49), after citing those varied and confused narrations: "The most correct of these statements is to say: Allah, may His praise be exalted, informed of the intention of Yusuf and the wife of the chief, each of them toward the other, were it not that Yusuf saw the proof of his Lord, which is a sign of Allah's signs that restrained him from committing the immorality which Yusuf had intended. It is possible that this sign was the image of Ya'qub, possible that it was the image of the king, and possible that the warning was in the verses which Allah mentioned in the Qur'an concerning fornication. There is no decisive proof for any one of these. The correct course is to say what Allah, blessed and exalted, has said, to believe in it, and to leave all else to its Knower." Shaykh al-Shinqiti said in Adwa' al-Bayan (3/68): "These statements which I have seen attributed to these scholars are of two kinds: one kind whose transmission has not been established from those to whom it is attributed by a sound chain, and there is no difficulty in discarding it. And another kind which has been established from some of those mentioned. As for whoever of them has something of that established, the apparent and dominant assumption, which competes with certainty, is that he only received it from the Isra'iliyyat, since there is no room for opinion in it, and not a little or a great deal of it has been traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ). From this you know that one should not dare to say of the Prophet of Allah Yusuf that he sat between the legs of a foreign disbelieving woman, intending to commit fornication with her, relying on such narrations—especially since these narrations contain signs of falsehood, such as the story of the palm which appeared to him four times, and in three of them he paid it no attention. For that, even if it were sound, contains the greatest deterrent for common sinners; so what do you think of the choicest of the prophets! Moreover, we have presented the evidence of the Qur'an for his innocence from several aspects, and we have clarified that the reality does not exceed one of two matters: either he never had any intention toward her at all, based on linking his intention to not seeing the proof, and he did see the proof; or his intention was the natural inclination restrained by piety. And Allah knows best."]].

As for the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Had it not been that he saw the proof of his Lord﴾: the answer to "law la" (had it not been) is omitted; its estimated meaning is: had it not been that he saw the proof of his Lord, he would have committed the disobedience.

﴿Thus, that We might avert from him evil and immorality﴾: "as-su'" (evil) is sin. It was said: "as-su'" is ugliness. And "al-fahsha'" (immorality) is fornication.

﴿Indeed, he was among Our chosen servants﴾: The people of Madinah and Kufah read ﴿al-mukhlasin﴾ with a fatha on the lam wherever there is no mention of religion after it; the Kufans added "mukhlasan" in Surat Maryam and read it with a fatha.

The meaning of ﴿al-mukhlasin﴾ with fatha is "those chosen for prophethood"; its proof is: ﴿Indeed, We made them sincere with a pure sincerity﴾ [Sad: 46].

The others read it with a kasra on the lam, meaning: those who make obedience and worship sincere for Allah.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 12, verses 25–26:**

﴿And they raced each other to the door.﴾ This was because when Yusuf saw the proof (burhan), he rose hastily toward the door of the house to flee. The woman followed him so that she could hold the door shut and prevent Yusuf from leaving. Yusuf got there first, but the woman caught up with him and seized his shirt from behind, pulling him back toward her so that he could not leave.

﴿And she tore his shirt﴾, that is, she ripped it, ﴿from behind﴾, that is, from the back. When they came out, they met the lord (al-Aziz), which is His saying:

﴿And they found her husband at the door.﴾ That is, they found the woman's husband, Qitfir, sitting at the door with a paternal cousin of Ra'il. When she saw him, she was afraid of him, and she spoke first to her husband, saying: ﴿"What is the punishment for one who intended evil against your wife?"﴾, meaning adultery (zina, illicit sexual intercourse). Then she feared that he would kill him, so she said: ﴿"Except that he be imprisoned"﴾, that is, confined, ﴿"or a painful punishment"﴾, that is, beaten with whips. When Yusuf heard her words,

﴿He said: "It was she who sought to seduce me."﴾ meaning, she demanded illicit intercourse from me, but I refused and fled.

It was also said: Yusuf had not intended to mention it, but when the woman said, "What is the punishment for one who intended evil against your wife?", he mentioned it, saying, "It was she who sought to seduce me."

﴿And a witness testified﴾, that is, a judge gave judgment, ﴿from among her own people.﴾ The scholars differed regarding this witness:

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak said: He was an infant in the cradle, whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, caused to speak.[[Narrated by Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir from them both. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/526.]] This is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Four spoke while they were infants: the son of the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter, the witness of Yusuf, the companion of Jurayj, and Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him."[[Narrated by Ibn Jarir in his Tafsir from Ibn Abbas: (16/55), and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad in full under numbers (2822–2825), Halabi edition, without raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ). Also Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, p. (40), from Mawarid al-Zam'an. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/65): "Narrated by Ahmad, al-Bazzar, and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir and al-Awsat, and in its chain is Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, who is trustworthy but became confused." It was also narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak from Abu Hurayrah (2/497), and he said: "This hadith has a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." al-Suyuti attributed it to al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, and Ibn Hajar added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Ya'la and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman. See: al-Kafi al-Shafi, p. (89). Shaykh Mahmud Shakir authenticated it in his commentary on al-Tabari, in the same place. See also: Fath al-Bari by Ibn Hajar: 6/480.]]

It was also said: That infant was the son of the woman's maternal aunt.

Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qatadah and Mujahid said: He was not an infant, but a wise man of sound judgment.[[See: al-Durr al-Manthur 4/526.]]

al-Suddi said: He was a paternal cousin of Ra'il.[[al-Tabari said in his Tafsir (2/59): "The correct view on this matter is the view of those who said he was an infant in the cradle, on account of the report we have mentioned from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he mentioned those who spoke in the cradle, and said that one of them was the companion of Yusuf."]] So he judged and said: ﴿"If her shirt is torn from the front"﴾, that is, from in front, ﴿"then she has spoken truly, and he is one of the liars."﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 12, verses 30–31:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And women in the city said﴾, and so on.

He means: the matter of Yusuf and the woman spread in the city, the city of Egypt. It was also said: the city of ʿAyn al-Shams. The women talked about it and said, and they were five women: the wife of the king's chamberlain (ḥājib) [[In "B": ṣāḥib.]], the wife of the master of the mounts, the wife of the baker, the wife of the cupbearer, and the wife of the jailer. This was reported by Muqatil.

It was also said: they were women from among the nobles of Egypt.

﴿The wife of the ʿAzīz is seeking to seduce her young man﴾, that is, her slave, the Canaanite, ﴿from himself﴾, that is, she seeks from her slave an act of immorality. ﴿She is consumed by love for him﴾, that is, she has become attached to him through love.

Al-Kalbi said: his love veiled her heart so that she could understand nothing other than him.

It was also said: she loved him until his love entered the *shaghaf* of her heart, that is, the inner part of her heart.

Al-Suddi said: the *shaghaf* is a thin membrane over the heart. He means: the love penetrated the skin until it reached the heart.

Al-Shaʿbi and al-Aʿraj [[In "B": al-Aʿmash.]] recited *shaʿafahā* with an unpointed ʿayn. Its meaning: love carried her away in every direction. From this comes *shaʿaf al-jibāl*, which means the peaks of the mountains.

﴿Indeed, we see her in clear error﴾, that is, manifest mistake. It was also said: the meaning is that she has abandoned what women like her ordinarily keep of chastity and modesty.

﴿When she heard﴾ Rāʿīl (of her plotting), ﴿of their scheming﴾, that is, of their words and their talk. This was said by Qatadah and al-Suddi.

Ibn Ishaq said: they said this only as a scheme against her, in order to make her show them Yusuf, for his beauty and his comeliness used to be described to them.

It was also said: she had revealed her secret to them and asked them to keep it, but they spread it. For this reason he called it a scheme.

﴿She sent for them﴾. Wahb said: she prepared a banquet and invited forty women, among them those who had blamed her.

﴿And she prepared﴾, that is, she readied, ﴿for them a *mutraka*﴾, that is, that on which one reclines.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah and Mujahid said: *mutaka* means food. It was called *mutaka* because when people of food sit, they recline on cushions, so food was called *mutaka* by way of metaphor. It is said: "We reclined at So-and-so's," meaning we ate. It is also said: *al-mutaka* is that on which one reclines for drinking, for conversation, or for eating. In the non-canonical readings (*shawādhdh*) it is also read *matkan* with the *tāʾ* sukūn.

They differed about its meaning. Ibn ʿAbbas said: [it is the citron. This is also reported from Mujahid. And it was said] [[Omitted from "A".]] it is the citron in Abyssinian (Ethiopian).

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it is *al-rabāward* (a kind of fruit or sweet).

ʿIkrimah said: it is everything that is cut with a knife.

Abu Zayd al-Ansari said: everything that is cut with a knife is, among the Arabs, called *mutk*, and *al-mutk* and *al-butk* (with *mīm* and *bāʾ*) mean cutting. So she decorated the banquet [with various colours] [[In "B": a house with kinds of.]] of fruits and foods, placed the cushions, and invited the women.

﴿And she gave﴾, that is, she handed, ﴿each one of them a knife﴾. So they began to eat the meat by cutting it with the knives.

﴿And she said﴾ to Yusuf, ﴿Come out before them﴾. This was because she had seated him in another room, and Yusuf came out before them.

ʿIkrimah said: the superiority of Yusuf over people in beauty was like the superiority of the full moon on its night over all the other stars.

It is related from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken up to the heaven, I saw Yusuf, like the full moon on its night."

[[Ibn Hajar said in *al-Kafi al-Shaf* (p. 89): "al-Tha'labi related it through Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi from Abu Saʿid. al-Ḥākim, al-Bayhaqi in *al-Dalāʾil*, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from this route at length, and Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi is weak."]]

Ishaq ibn Abi Farwah said: when Yusuf walked through the alleys of Egypt, the radiance of his face would be seen reflected on the walls.

﴿So when they saw him, they magnified him﴾, that is, they glorified him. Abu al-ʿĀliyah said: his matter overwhelmed them and they were astonished. It was also said: *akbarnahu* means they menstruated because of him, due to his beauty. [[This interpretation is also weakened by al-Ṭabarī (16/76–77) and Ibn ʿAṭiyyah in *al-Muḥarrar al-Wajīz* (7/495–496).]] And this is not sound.

﴿And they cut﴾, that is, they slashed with the knives they had, ﴿their hands﴾, while they thought they were cutting the citron. They did not feel the pain, because their hearts were occupied with Yusuf.

Mujahid said: they perceived nothing but the blood.

The others recited it with the *yāʾ* omitted, because it occurs frequently on the tongues and in agreement with the written text (*al-kitāb*, the Qur'anic orthography).

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 12, verses 30–31:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And women in the city said﴾, and so on.

He means: the matter of Yusuf and the woman spread in the city, the city of Egypt. It was also said: the city of ʿAyn al-Shams. The women talked about it and said, and they were five women: the wife of the king's chamberlain (ḥājib) [[In "B": ṣāḥib.]], the wife of the master of the mounts, the wife of the baker, the wife of the cupbearer, and the wife of the jailer. This was reported by Muqatil.

It was also said: they were women from among the nobles of Egypt.

﴿The wife of the ʿAzīz is seeking to seduce her young man﴾, that is, her slave, the Canaanite, ﴿from himself﴾, that is, she seeks from her slave an act of immorality. ﴿She is consumed by love for him﴾, that is, she has become attached to him through love.

Al-Kalbi said: his love veiled her heart so that she could understand nothing other than him.

It was also said: she loved him until his love entered the *shaghaf* of her heart, that is, the inner part of her heart.

Al-Suddi said: the *shaghaf* is a thin membrane over the heart. He means: the love penetrated the skin until it reached the heart.

Al-Shaʿbi and al-Aʿraj [[In "B": al-Aʿmash.]] recited *shaʿafahā* with an unpointed ʿayn. Its meaning: love carried her away in every direction. From this comes *shaʿaf al-jibāl*, which means the peaks of the mountains.

﴿Indeed, we see her in clear error﴾, that is, manifest mistake. It was also said: the meaning is that she has abandoned what women like her ordinarily keep of chastity and modesty.

﴿When she heard﴾ Rāʿīl (of her plotting), ﴿of their scheming﴾, that is, of their words and their talk. This was said by Qatadah and al-Suddi.

Ibn Ishaq said: they said this only as a scheme against her, in order to make her show them Yusuf, for his beauty and his comeliness used to be described to them.

It was also said: she had revealed her secret to them and asked them to keep it, but they spread it. For this reason he called it a scheme.

﴿She sent for them﴾. Wahb said: she prepared a banquet and invited forty women, among them those who had blamed her.

﴿And she prepared﴾, that is, she readied, ﴿for them a *mutraka*﴾, that is, that on which one reclines.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah and Mujahid said: *mutaka* means food. It was called *mutaka* because when people of food sit, they recline on cushions, so food was called *mutaka* by way of metaphor. It is said: "We reclined at So-and-so's," meaning we ate. It is also said: *al-mutaka* is that on which one reclines for drinking, for conversation, or for eating. In the non-canonical readings (*shawādhdh*) it is also read *matkan* with the *tāʾ* sukūn.

They differed about its meaning. Ibn ʿAbbas said: [it is the citron. This is also reported from Mujahid. And it was said] [[Omitted from "A".]] it is the citron in Abyssinian (Ethiopian).

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it is *al-rabāward* (a kind of fruit or sweet).

ʿIkrimah said: it is everything that is cut with a knife.

Abu Zayd al-Ansari said: everything that is cut with a knife is, among the Arabs, called *mutk*, and *al-mutk* and *al-butk* (with *mīm* and *bāʾ*) mean cutting. So she decorated the banquet [with various colours] [[In "B": a house with kinds of.]] of fruits and foods, placed the cushions, and invited the women.

﴿And she gave﴾, that is, she handed, ﴿each one of them a knife﴾. So they began to eat the meat by cutting it with the knives.

﴿And she said﴾ to Yusuf, ﴿Come out before them﴾. This was because she had seated him in another room, and Yusuf came out before them.

ʿIkrimah said: the superiority of Yusuf over people in beauty was like the superiority of the full moon on its night over all the other stars.

It is related from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken up to the heaven, I saw Yusuf, like the full moon on its night."

[[Ibn Hajar said in *al-Kafi al-Shaf* (p. 89): "al-Tha'labi related it through Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi from Abu Saʿid. al-Ḥākim, al-Bayhaqi in *al-Dalāʾil*, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from this route at length, and Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi is weak."]]

Ishaq ibn Abi Farwah said: when Yusuf walked through the alleys of Egypt, the radiance of his face would be seen reflected on the walls.

﴿So when they saw him, they magnified him﴾, that is, they glorified him. Abu al-ʿĀliyah said: his matter overwhelmed them and they were astonished. It was also said: *akbarnahu* means they menstruated because of him, due to his beauty. [[This interpretation is also weakened by al-Ṭabarī (16/76–77) and Ibn ʿAṭiyyah in *al-Muḥarrar al-Wajīz* (7/495–496).]] And this is not sound.

It is possible that this was a severing, and it is possible that it was a slash or scratch. There is no statement more correct than accepting the apparent sense of the revelation."]].

﴿She said﴾, meaning Ra'il: ﴿That is the one you blamed me for﴾, i.e., for loving him. Then she openly stated what she had done, saying: ﴿I certainly sought to seduce him, but he refused﴾, i.e., he held back. She spoke openly because she knew that the women had no reason to blame her, since they had been affected by what had affected her when they saw him. So they said to him: "Obey your mistress." Then Ra'il said: ﴿And if he does not do what I command him﴾, meaning, if he does not comply with what I call him to, ﴿he will surely be imprisoned﴾, i.e., he will certainly be punished with confinement, ﴿and he will surely be among the humiliated﴾, meaning among the abased.

The emphatic nun (nun al-tawkid) may be pronounced heavy or light. The pause (waqf) on ﴿لَيُسْجَنَنَّ﴾ is made with the nun, because it is doubled (heavy). On ﴿وَلَيَكُونًا﴾ it is made with the alif, because it is light. It resembles the nun of i'rab (grammatical inflection) in nouns, as in your saying: "I saw a man (rajulan)." When you pause, you say: "I saw a man" with an alif. A similar example is: ﴿Surely We shall seize him by the forelock, a lying, sinful forelock﴾ (al-'Alaq, 15–16).

Yusuf (peace be upon him) chose prison over disobedience when the woman threatened him.

﴿He said, "My Lord"﴾, meaning: O my Lord. ﴿"The prison is dearer to me than what they invite me to"﴾. It was said: the invitation came from her alone, but he attributed it to all of them, moving from explicit speech (tasrih) to allusion (ta'rid).

It was also said: all of them invited him to themselves.

Ya'qub alone read ﴿al-sijnu﴾ with a fatha on the sin. The rest of the readers (al-'ammah) read it with a kasra. (Qira'ah: a canonical mode of Qur'anic recitation.)

It was said: had he not said "the prison is dearer to me," he would not have been tested with the prison. It is best for a person to ask Allah for well-being (al-'afiyah).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿"And unless You turn their scheming away from me, I shall incline toward them and become one of the ignorant"﴾. ﴿Asbu﴾ means: I incline toward them and follow them. One says: "So-and-so inclined (saba) toward such-and-such, inclines (yasbu) with sabwan, sububan and sabwah, when he leans toward it and longs for it."

﴿"And I would be among the ignorant"﴾. In this is evidence that a believer who commits a sin, commits it out of ignorance (jahalah).

﴿So his Lord responded to him (fastajaba lahu)﴾, meaning: He answered him.

﴿...so He turned their scheming away from him. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [to his supplication] [[Omitted from manuscript "A".]], the All-Knowing of their deceit.

﴿Then it became apparent to them﴾, meaning: to al-'Aziz and his companions in opinion. That is because they had intended to limit the matter of Yusuf to merely turning away (from the woman). Then it occurred to them to imprison him.

﴿After they had seen the signs﴾ indicating Yusuf's innocence: the tearing of the shirt from behind, the speech of the infant, the women cutting their hands and the loss of their reason. ﴿They imprisoned him for a while﴾, until a period in which they would carry out their opinion.

ʿAṭāʾ said: until people's talk about the matter ceased.

ʿIkrimah said: seven years.

al-Kalbi said: five years.

al-Suddi said: That was because the woman said to her husband: "This Hebrew slave has disgraced me among the people. He tells them that I solicited him. Either you permit me to go out and apologize to the people, or you imprison him." So he imprisoned him. It is also mentioned that Allah, exalted is He, made that imprisonment a purification for Yusuf, peace be upon him, from his inclination toward the woman. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/93.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: Yusuf stumbled three stumbles: when he inclined toward her and was imprisoned; when he said to the one who would be saved, "Mention me to your lord," and so he remained in prison several years; and when he said to the brothers, "Indeed, you are thieves," and they said, "If he steals, a brother of his stole before him." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/93.]]

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/93.]]

﴿And there entered the prison with him two young men.﴾ They were two slaves belonging to al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid ibn Shirwan al-Amliqi, the great king of Egypt.[[In "B": "al-Walid ibn Thuwan al-Amliqi."]] One of them was his baker and keeper of his food, and the other was his cupbearer and keeper of his drink. The king became angry with them both and imprisoned them.

The cause of this was that a group of people from Egypt wanted to plot against the king and assassinate him. They promised these two a sum of money if they would poison the king's food and drink. They agreed, but then the cupbearer backed out, while the baker accepted the bribe and poisoned the food. When the food and drink were brought, the cupbearer said: "Do not eat, O king, for the food is poisoned." The baker said: "Do not drink, for the drink is poisoned."

The king said to the cupbearer: "Drink," and he drank it and it did him no harm. He said to the baker: "Eat from your food." He refused,[[In "B": "for I have tested it."]] so the king had that food given to an animal, and it ate it and died. The king then ordered that they both be imprisoned.

When Yusuf entered the prison, he began to spread his knowledge, saying: "I interpret dreams." One of the two young men said to his companion: "Come, let us test this Hebrew servant." They came to him and asked him about dreams without having actually seen anything. Ibn Mas'ud said: "They had seen nothing; they only pretended to dream in order to test Yusuf."

Others said: "Rather, they had truly seen dreams." Yusuf saw them distressed and asked them about their situation. They mentioned that they were the king's companions whom he had imprisoned, and that they had seen a dream that had troubled them. Yusuf said: "Tell me what you saw," and they related it to him.

﴿One of them said﴾, namely the cupbearer, ﴿"Indeed I saw myself pressing wine"﴾, meaning grapes. He called the grapes "wine" by the name of what they would become, just as one says: "So-and-so is baking bricks," meaning he is firing mud into bricks for kilns. It was also said that "khamr" in the dialect of Oman means grapes. He said: "I saw in a dream that I was in an orchard, and there was a vine stem bearing three clusters of grapes. I picked them, and the king's cup was in my hand; I pressed them into it and gave the king to drink, and he drank it."

﴿And the other said﴾, namely the baker: ﴿"Indeed I saw myself carrying bread on my head, of which the birds were eating"﴾. He said: "I saw in a dream that on my head were three baskets containing bread and various kinds of food, and birds of prey were pecking at them."

﴿"Inform us of its interpretation"﴾, that is, explain to us its meaning, its interpretation (ta'wil), and what the outcome of this dream will be.

﴿"Indeed we see you to be among the good-doers"﴾, that is, among those knowledgeable in the interpretation of dreams, for ihsan here means knowledge.

It is related that al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim was asked about the words ﴿"Indeed we see you to be among the good-doers"﴾: what was his good-doing? He said: "When a person fell ill in the prison, he would visit him and attend to him; when someone was crowded, he would make room for him; when someone was in need, he would gather something for him. Along with this, he exerted himself in worship and would spend the whole night in prayer."[[This is the view preferred by Abu Ja'far al-Tabari: 16/100.]]

It was also said[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 16/99 from Qatada, and he said after it: "The most correct of the views in our judgment is the view we mentioned from al-Dahhak and Qatada."]] that when he entered the prison, he found in it people whose trials had become severe, whose hope had been cut off, and whose grief had lengthened. So he began to console them, saying: "Be glad and be patient, and you will be rewarded." They would say: "May God bless you, O young man. How beautiful is your face, your character and your speech! Blessing has come to us through your presence. Who are you, O young man?" He said: "I am Yusuf, son of the chosen one of God, Ya'qub, son of the sacrificed one of God, Ishaq,[[See the note (1) above on p. (215) concerning the sacrificed one.]] son of the friend of God, Ibrahim." The jailer said to him: "O young man, by God, if I could, I would release you, but I will treat you well as a guest, and you may stay in whichever part of the prison you wish."

It is also related that when the two young men saw Yusuf, they said to him: "We have loved you since we saw you." Yusuf said to them: "I beseech you by God not to love me, for by God no one has ever loved me without a trial befalling me because of that love. My aunt loved me, and a trial came upon me; then my father loved me, and I was thrown into the well; and the wife of the Aziz loved me, and I was imprisoned."[[The manuscript page break "182/b" occurs here.]] When they related the dream to him, Yusuf disliked to interpret it for them, because he knew it contained something disagreeable for one of them. So he turned away from their question and turned to other matters, displaying the miracle and calling to monotheism.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 16/102; al-Suyuti also attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim from Ibn Ishaq.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 12, verse 37:

﴿He said: "No food will come to you as your provision but I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you."﴾ It has been said: he meant by it during sleep. He says: "No food will come to you as your provision during your sleep, ﴿but I will inform you of its interpretation﴾ while awake."

It has also been said: he meant by it while awake. He says: "No food will come to you from your dwellings as your provision, that you will be fed and eat, but I will inform you of its interpretation: its quantity, its colour, and the time at which it reaches you."

﴿Before it comes to you﴾: before it reaches you. And what food you ate, how much you ate, and when you ate it. This is like the miracle of Jesus, peace be upon him, when he said: ﴿And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 49]. They both said: "This is the practice of the 'arrafin (diviners) and the kahanah (soothsayers)" [[al-'Arraf: one who claims to know hidden matters through preliminary signs, verbal or practical, by which he infers their occurrence, such as someone who is suspected of theft and is identified as the thief. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah made it a term for the soothsayer, the astrologer, the geomancer and the like. The kahin (soothsayer) is one who claims knowledge of the unseen, such as reporting what will happen on earth while relying on a cause. Its origin is the jinn eavesdropping on the speech of the angels and casting it into the ear of the soothsayer. This is a form of claiming knowledge of the unseen, which Islam has forbidden, since none knows the unseen except Allah. For a detailed treatment see: 'Alim al-Ghayb wa al-Shahadah fi al-Tasawwur al-Islami, by Uthman Jum'ah Dumairiyyah, pp. (117-131).]], "From where do you have this knowledge?" He said: "I am not a soothsayer, but ﴿that﴾ knowledge is ﴿part of what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have abandoned the creed of a people who do not believe in Allah and who deny the Hereafter, they are disbelievers.﴾" The repetition of ﴿they﴾ is for emphasis.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 12, verses 38–39:

﴿And I have followed the religion of my fathers: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob﴾ He showed that he was from the offspring of the prophets. ﴿It is not for us﴾ meaning: it is not befitting for us, ﴿to associate anything with Allah﴾. Its meaning: Allah has protected us from associating partners with Him. ﴿That﴾ monotheism and knowledge ﴿is of the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind﴾, meaning the guidance He has made clear for them. ﴿Yet most of mankind are not grateful﴾. Then he invited the two of them to Islam, saying:

﴿O two companions of the prison﴾. He called them "two companions of the prison" because they were in it, just as the inhabitants of Paradise are called "companions of Paradise" and the inhabitants of Hell are called "companions of the Fire". ﴿Are many lords dispersed better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ That is, many gods of different kinds: this one is of gold, this one of silver, this one of iron, this one is high, this one is middling, this one is low, differing from one another, neither harming nor benefiting. ﴿The One who has no equal﴾. Al-Qahhar (the Subduer): the one who prevails over all things. Then he explained the powerlessness of the idols, saying:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 12, verses 38–39:

﴿And I have followed the religion of my fathers: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob﴾ He showed that he was from the offspring of the prophets. ﴿It is not for us﴾ meaning: it is not befitting for us, ﴿to associate anything with Allah﴾. Its meaning: Allah has protected us from associating partners with Him. ﴿That﴾ monotheism and knowledge ﴿is of the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind﴾, meaning the guidance He has made clear for them. ﴿Yet most of mankind are not grateful﴾. Then he invited the two of them to Islam, saying:

﴿O two companions of the prison﴾. He called them "two companions of the prison" because they were in it, just as the inhabitants of Paradise are called "companions of Paradise" and the inhabitants of Hell are called "companions of the Fire". ﴿Are many lords dispersed better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ That is, many gods of different kinds: this one is of gold, this one of silver, this one of iron, this one is high, this one is middling, this one is low, differing from one another, neither harming nor benefiting. ﴿The One who has no equal﴾. Al-Qahhar (the Subduer): the one who prevails over all things. Then he explained the powerlessness of the idols, saying:

﴿مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ "What you worship other than Him," i.e., other than Allah. It is expressed in the plural, though the address began in the dual, because he intended all the people of the prison and everyone who is in the same state of polytheism (shirk) as the two of them. ﴿إِلَّا أَسْمَاءً سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا﴾ "are only names you have named" as gods and lords, empty of meaning, with no reality behind those names. ﴿أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِنْ سُلْطَانٍ﴾ "you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority," meaning no proof or evidence. ﴿إِنِ الْحُكْمُ﴾ "Judgment belongs" means the decision, the command and the prohibition. ﴿إِلَّا لِلَّهِ أَمَرَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ ذَلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ﴾ "belongs only to Allah. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the upright religion," meaning the straight one. ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ "But most of mankind do not know." Then he interpreted their dream, saying: ﴿يَا صَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَمَّا أَحَدُكُمَا﴾ "O two fellow prisoners! As for one of you,"

﴿يَا صَاحِبَيِ السِّجْنِ أَمَّا أَحَدُكُمَا﴾ "O two fellow prisoners! As for one of you," he is the cupbearer, ﴿فَيَسْقِي رَبَّهُ﴾ "he will give his lord [meaning the king]" ﴿خَمْرًا﴾ "wine to drink." The three clusters were three days. He will remain in prison for three days, and then after three days the king will summon him and restore him to the position he had held. ﴿وَأَمَّا الْآخَرُ﴾ "As for the other," meaning the one with the food, the king will summon him after three days, and the three baskets were three days. He will remain in prison, then he will bring him out ﴿فَيُصْلَبُ فَتَأْكُلُ الطَّيْرُ مِنْ رَأْسِهِ﴾ "and he will be crucified, and birds will eat from his head."

Ibn Mas'ud said: When the two of them heard Yusuf's words, they said, "We saw nothing; we were only playing." Yusuf said: ﴿قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ الَّذِي فِيهِ تَسْتَفْتِيَانِ﴾ "The matter about which you both inquire has been decided" [[Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (4/540) to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh.]], meaning: the matter about which you ask has been concluded, and Allah's judgment that I told you of has become binding upon you, whether you saw it or did not see it.

﴿وَقَالَ﴾ "And he said," meaning Yusuf at that point, ﴿لِلَّذِي ظَنَّ﴾ "to the one who thought," i.e., knew, ﴿أَنَّهُ نَاجٍ مِنْهُمَا﴾ "that he was going to be saved of the two," and he was the cupbearer, ﴿اذْكُرْنِي عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ﴾ "Mention me to your lord," meaning your master the king, and say to him: "There is a young man in the prison, wrongfully imprisoned, whose confinement has lasted long."

﴿فَأَنْسَاهُ الشَّيْطَانُ ذِكْرَ رَبِّهِ﴾ "But Satan caused him to forget the mention of his lord." It was said: Satan made the cupbearer forget mentioning Yusuf to the king. Its meaning is: Satan made him forget to mention it to his lord.

Ibn 'Abbas said, and most of the scholars agree: Satan made Yusuf forget the mention of his lord when he sought deliverance from someone other than Allah and sought help from a created being. That was a lapse that came upon Yusuf from Satan [[Abu Hayyan preferred that the pronoun refers to the cupbearer, which is the first opinion, and Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah also preferred it for several reasons. He said: "...Rather, Satan made the one who was saved of the two of them forget the mention of his lord, and this is the correct view, for it agrees with his saying, 'Mention me to your lord.' Allah the Exalted says, 'Satan made him forget the mention of his lord,' and the pronoun returns to the nearest antecedent when there is no evidence to the contrary. Yusuf did not forget the mention of his lord; rather he was constantly mindful of his lord... Then after several points he said: It is clear that His saying 'Satan made him forget the mention of his lord' means: Satan made the youth forget to mention this to his lord, and the one who forgot the mention of Yusuf to his lord... It is clarified that the one who forgot his lord was the youth and not Yusuf by His saying afterward: 'And the one who was saved of the two said, after a while, I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth,' and His saying, 'after a while,' is evidence that he forgot and then remembered." See: Daqa'iq al-Tafsir by Ibn Taymiyyah: 3/259-263, and consult al-Bahr al-Muhit by Abu Hayyan: 5/311-312.]].

﴿فَلَبِثَ﴾ "So he remained," meaning he stayed, ﴿فِي السِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ﴾ "in prison for several years." The scholars differed about the meaning of "bid'" (a few). Mujahid said: between three and seven.

Qatadah said: between three and nine.

Ibn 'Abbas said: fewer than ten.

Most of the commentators hold that "bid'" in this verse means seven years, and he had stayed there five years before that, so the total was twelve years.

Wahb said: Ayyub was afflicted for seven years, Yusuf was left in prison for seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar was punished and transformed among the beasts for seven years [[al-Tabari said in his tafsir (16/115): "The correct view regarding 'bid'' is from three to nine, up to ten, and it cannot be less than three. Likewise, what exceeds the decade up to a hundred, and what exceeds a hundred, cannot be described as 'bid''."]].

Malik ibn Dinar said: When Yusuf said to the cupbearer, "Mention me to your lord," it was said to him: "O Yusuf, you have taken other than Me as a trustee; I will surely prolong your imprisonment." Yusuf wept and said: "O Lord, the multitude of trials has made my heart forget; I spoke a word, and I will not return to it" [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir: 16/111.]].

Al-Hasan said: Jibril entered upon Yusuf in the prison. When Yusuf saw him, he recognized him and said to him: "O brother of those who warn, why do I see you among the sinners?" Jibril said to him: "O purest of the pure, the Lord of the worlds sends you His greetings and says to you: 'Were you not ashamed before Me, that you sought intercession from human beings? By My might, I will keep you in prison for several years.'" Yusuf said: "And is He pleased with me in that?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then I do not mind."

Ka'b said: Jibril said to Yusuf: "Allah the Exalted says: Who created you?" He said: "Allah." He said: "Who made you beloved to your father?" He said: "Allah." He said: "Who saved you from the distress of the well?" He said: "Allah." He said: "Who taught you the interpretation of dreams?" He said: "Allah." He said: "Who turned away from you evil and immorality?" He said: "Allah." He said: "Then how did you seek intercession from a human being like yourself?" It would have been better for him to rely upon Allah and not say "Mention me to your lord." When he failed to rely upon his Lord, he was requited with a stay in prison for several years.
